name: Quicky Scroll – 3D Interactive Scrolling Animations
author: mosshive

sections.description:
Turn a short video into a full-screen section that plays as the visitor scrolls, with captions appearing along the way.

  • Frames: a set of same-size images, usually made from a video with Video to Frames. Pick a saved set under Frames → Use a frame set, or choose images from the Media Library with “Choose frames”. They play in order with a soft crossfade between neighbours.
  • Preview in the editor: drag the Preview slider or press Play to watch the frames without leaving the page.
  • Captions: each “Quicky Scroll Caption” holds ordinary blocks (headings, paragraphs, buttons). Add one with “Add caption”; the scroll is shared out evenly between them.
  • Caption looks: five positions, three styles (plain, panel, frosted glass) and four entrance effects (slide, fade, zoom, blur).
  • Animation: scroll speed, smoothness, play in reverse, fill the screen or show the whole frame, fade out into the next section.
  • Phones and tablets: a separate portrait frame set for screens up to 781 px, a focus point for wide footage on tall screens, a faster scroll speed, a different caption position and lighter loading (every second frame).
  • Patterns: ready-made layouts under Patterns → Quicky Scroll (three-caption story, centred title reveal, product spotlight).
  • Getting Started guide: Dashboard → Quicky Scroll walks through making frames, adding the block and every setting, with fixes for common problems.

Visitors who prefer reduced motion get the frames without easing. Without JavaScript the first frame and the first caption show. Frames load only when the block is near the screen, and phones with Data Saver on get the lighter set automatically.

Privacy

Quicky Scroll doesn’t track visitors, set cookies or contact any outside service. The Video to Frames converter works entirely in your browser: the video never leaves your computer, and only the finished frames are uploaded, to your own Media Library.

Video to Frames

Dashboard → Quicky Scroll → Video to Frames turns a short video into numbered JPG frames.

  1. Choose an MP4 (H.264) or WebM video, up to 50 MB. Play it and scrub through it on the page.
  2. Trim: drag the two handles on the trim bar under the player to keep only the part you want, or drag the highlighted part to move it along. “Set start here” and “Set end here” use the player’s position, and Play stays inside the kept part.
  3. Crop: choose a shape (16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 4:5, 9:16 or free), then drag the box to choose what to keep and drag a corner to resize. Arrow keys nudge the box. A 9:16 crop makes a set for phones.
  4. Choose the number of frames (10 to 300), the frame size and the JPG quality. The page estimates the total size as you go.
  5. Click “Make frames”, check them with the preview slider, then “Add to Media Library” (saved as a frame set) or “Download ZIP”.
  6. “Use in a new page” opens a new page with a Quicky Scroll Block already using the set (a new post for users who can’t create pages).

The video is processed in your browser and is never uploaded; only the finished frames are. If your browser pauses the video while you’re on another tab, making frames waits and carries on when you come back. Frames added by the converter only get the small thumbnail size, not every image size, to save disk space. Your last frame count, size, quality and crop shape are remembered.

Why the limits: the browser holds the whole video and every finished frame in memory, so 50 MB and 300 frames keep it reliable on ordinary laptops. A scroll animation rarely needs more than 10 to 20 seconds of footage, so shorten a longer video in a video editor before choosing it, then fine-tune with the trim bar.

“Remove from list” only forgets a set. Its images stay in the Media Library; delete them there if you no longer need them. A set can be removed by the person who made it or by an editor.

Requirements

WordPress 6.5 or later with the block editor, and a current browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari) for the converter. Nothing else.
sections.installation:
1. Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose quicky-scroll.zip, then Activate.
  2. Open Dashboard → Quicky Scroll for the Getting Started guide.
  3. Make frames with Quicky Scroll → Video to Frames, or upload your own numbered frames to the Media Library.
  4. In the editor, insert “Quicky Scroll Block” (in the Quicky Scroll group) and pick a frame set.

Tip: 60 to 150 frames, around 1600 to 1920 px wide at JPG quality 75 to 85, keep the page light and smooth. For phones, add a 9:16 set of about 1080 px under Phones & tablets → Phone frames.
sections.faq:
Is my video uploaded anywhere?

No. The converter reads and cuts the video in your browser. Only the finished JPG frames are uploaded, to your own Media Library, and only when you click “Add to Media Library”. Nothing is sent to any other service.

Which videos can I use?

MP4 (H.264) or WebM, up to 50 MB. iPhone videos are often HEVC, which some browsers can’t open: export the clip as MP4 (H.264), or try the converter in Safari.

How many frames should I make?

60 to 150 frames around 1600 to 1920 px wide suit most animations. More frames look smoother but take longer to load.

Can I use frames I made somewhere else?

Yes. Upload numbered images (frame-001, frame-002 …) to the Media Library and pick them with “Choose frames”. They play in file-name order.

Does it work with my theme?

It works with block themes and with classic themes that use the block editor. Quicky Scroll Block goes into any page or post (and into templates in a block theme).

My header covers the captions.

Select the block and set Sticky header offset, under More options, to your header’s height in pixels.

What happens to my frames if I delete the plugin?

Deleting the plugin forgets the saved frame sets and its own settings. The frame images stay in the Media Library, and pages keep their content, so you can remove the images yourself if you no longer need them.

Why does the converter start a background worker?

Turning each frame into a JPG happens in a Web Worker built from the converter’s own script, so the page stays responsive while frames are made. It loads nothing from outside your site.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First release.
  • Quicky Scroll Block and its caption block: frames that play as visitors scroll, with captions, five caption positions, three caption styles and four entrance effects.
  • Animation settings: scroll speed, smoothness, play in reverse, fill the screen or show the whole frame, shade strength, accent colour and fade-out.
  • Phones and tablets: a separate portrait frame set, focus point, scroll speed, caption position and lighter loading.
  • Video to Frames converter with a trim bar, cropping, a size estimate, “Add to Media Library”, “Download ZIP” and “Use in a new page”.
  • Getting Started guide and ready-made patterns.
